assumptions.source: synthetic, seeded; no real user data
assumptions.income: lognormal around INR 90,000, CV 0.04, 0% chance of a 45% income drop
assumptions.discretionary: lognormal around INR 22,000 (CV 0.1), correlation 0.4 with income
assumptions.realized: held-out test months 31-36 (drawn from test_seed), plan fitted on months 1-30

method.name: joint_month_bootstrap
method.description: Point = median of last 12 months per stream; whole-month residuals (income, essential, discretionary together) resampled with replacement from the last 24 months; 2000 paths; 80% PI = P10-P90.

sequences.label: Status quo
sequences.description: No cuts, no extra payments, no new savings.

sequences.label: Debt first
sequences.description: Cut discretionary 20%; send all cash above reserve + 50% of monthly essentials to the highest-APR debt.

sequences.label: Save first
sequences.description: Fixed monthly savings contribution sized to reach the goal by its deadline

sequences.label: Reserve, then debt
sequences.description: Cut discretionary 20%; first build reserve + a volatility buffer (at least the debt_first margin; 1.65 sd of monthly net cash flow x sqrt(6 months)), then send the surplus to debt.

plan.rationale: On the P50 forecast alone the best sequence is Debt first (objective INR 128,478, shortfall risk 0%). Among sequences with shortfall risk <= 10%, Debt first has the best objective (INR 128,478, risk 0%). Uncertainty did not change the choice.
